description: The line plot illustrates the performance of three datasets—20NG, IMDB, and NIPS—measured by the NPMI (Normalized Pointwise Mutual Information) metric as a function of the “weight of negative sampling,” which ranges from 0.5 to 3.0 on the x-axis. The y-axis represents NPMI values, scaled from 0.18 to 0.42, with a break indicated between 0.22 and 0.38 to accommodate the visual separation of the IMDB line from the others. The 20NG dataset (black squares connected by solid lines) starts at approximately NPMI = 0.37 at weight 0.5, rises slightly to 0.38 at weight 1.5, dips to 0.37 at weight 2.0, and ends at 0.38 at weight 3.0. The IMDB dataset (red circles) begins at NPMI ≈ 0.19 at weight 0.5, dips to 0.185 at weight 1.0, peaks at 0.195 at weight 1.5, drops again to 0.19 at weight 2.0, and stabilizes at 0.19 at weight 3.0. The NIPS dataset (blue triangles) starts at NPMI ≈ 0.40 at weight 0.5, peaks at 0.41 at weight 1.0, remains flat until weight 1.5, then declines slightly to 0.405 at weight 2.0 and 0.40 at weight 3.0. All three lines exhibit relatively stable trends with minor fluctuations across the range of negative sampling weights.
